lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Hello Rosa, it's Jean. Do you have a few minutes for our call?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hi Jean. Give me one second... okay, I'm here.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Before we start, is there anything on your mind you want to make sure we get to today?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Actually, I had a question about my blood work.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Are you feeling okay this week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Hanging in there.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I see.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: So last time your goal was to walk 20 minutes on 5 days. How did that go?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Well, good! I didn't miss a day.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You need to walk every day, no excuses.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: It rained almost every afternoon.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: How do you want to handle the walking going forward?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'm not sure.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Just get out there, even when it's hot.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I already bought new sneakers.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: What would make it easier next week?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I think I can do 20 minutes if it's early. My neighbor started doing it with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Some people walk inside the mall early, before the stores open. It's cool and it's flat.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Maybe.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: It's been a mixed week.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I could walk at the mall, it's air conditioned. Some days are better than others.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Three 10-minute walks count the same as one 30-minute walk.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I really want to feel like myself again. It's just me and my husband now, so it's easier.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You have to make this a priority.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Okay.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: You'd rather start small and actually stick with it.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Mm-hmm.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I know I can do it, I did it before.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: If the rain gets in the way again, what's your backup plan?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: I'll ask my son to come with me.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Let me make sure I got it. This week you did it 5 out of 5 days, the hard part was work, and next week you're going to walk 10 minutes on 4 days. Did I miss anything?

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: That's it exactly.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: I'll text you midweek to see how it's going, and we'll talk again in two weeks.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Can we do a little later? I have an appointment.

lines.speaker: coach
lines.text: Okay Rosa, have a good rest of your day.

lines.speaker: participant
lines.text: Thank you, talk soon.

flags.reason: Participant's blood work question was raised and never addressed or deferred to a follow-up.
'You need to walk every day, no excuses' is directive and pushes without permission after she reported success.
'Just get out there, even when it's hot' ignores her rain barrier and pushes activity despite heat.
'You have to make this a priority' imposes priority rather than eliciting her own motivation she had just voiced.
Recap says 10 minutes on 4 days, but Rosa agreed to 20 minutes on early walks; plan was misrepresented.

score.summary: Rosa reported full adherence and offered real ideas (early walks, mall, neighbor, son as backup), but the coach repeatedly persuaded with directives and never addressed her blood work question. The closing recap also misstated her agreed plan, so the session shifted from her change talk toward coach-driven goals.
strengths: Open question at line 12 invited Rosa to choose how to handle walking.
Line 29 open question on a backup plan for rain helped her generate her own solution.
Line 26 complex reflection captured her preference for starting small.
coaching_tips: Replace 'You need to walk every day, no excuses' (line 10) and 'You have to make this a priority' (line 24) with reflections that name her stated desire to feel like herself.
Address Rosa's blood work question at line 4 or schedule it explicitly before moving to goals.
Check the recap at line 31 against her words: she proposed 20-minute early walks, so confirm the plan rather than restating it.
